overridesNotes.postcss@<8.5.23: GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 XSS via unescaped </style> in stringify, plus GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q (<=8.5.11), GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 (<=8.5.17) and GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp (<=8.5.22) arbitrary .map file disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL when `from` is unset. GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp is an incomplete-fix follow-up to GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q, which is why the previous 8.5.19 target went stale and had to be lifted to 8.5.23 — the pin itself was holding a still-vulnerable version. next 16.2.x still pins postcss 8.4.31 exactly, and @tailwindcss/postcss allows ^8.5.6, so this override is what lifts next's copy. Do NOT retarget this at next 16.3: 16.3.0-preview.9 pins postcss 8.5.10, which is still vulnerable to every sourceMappingURL advisory — so the previous 'remove when next 16.3 stable lands' trigger was wrong. 8.5.23 is 11 days old, clearing the 7-day quarantine. Remove only when next's own pinned postcss is >=8.5.23.
overridesNotes.postcss>nanoid: SECURITY: GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 — nanoid's custom generators loop indefinitely when size is zero. The advisory's fixed boundary moved: it first shipped as <3.3.17, and the 3.3.17 pin recorded here cleared it at the time, but the range was later corrected to <3.3.18 and 3.3.17 became vulnerable in turn — so this pin had gone stale and was itself holding the vulnerability, the same failure mode described in the postcss and brace-expansion notes. Raised to 3.3.18. Sole path is apps/homepage -> postcss@8.5.23 -> nanoid, and postcss@8.5.23 declares ^3.3.16, so 3.3.18 is already inside the parent's range — a resolution pin, not a forced upgrade. Scoped to postcss ON PURPOSE rather than a bare key: nanoid 5.x is a separate ESM-only major and the advisory also covers >=4.0.0 <5.1.6, so a flat key would rewrite any future 4.x/5.x copy down onto the 3.x line. 3.3.18 published 2026-08-07 and cleared the 7-day quarantine on 2026-08-14, so it installed unaided — no escape hatch needed, .npmrc and pnpm-workspace.yaml untouched. Remove when postcss's own ^3.3.16 resolves >=3.3.18 with no override.
overridesNotes.@modelcontextprotocol/sdk>@hono/node-ser: GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9 path traversal in serve-static on Windows via encoded backslash (%5C), fixed in 2.0.5. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0 is the LATEST published SDK and pins @hono/node-server ^1.19.9, so the fix is a major outside its range and no parent upgrade exists at all. 1.x -> 2.x is a major (Node >=20, changed serve() signature) but is unobservable here: the consuming modules (server/express.js, server/streamableHttp.js) are never imported — apps/web loads only server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js and server/mcp.js — and the advisory is Windows-only while the runtime is a Linux container. Peer hono ^4 is satisfied by our pinned 4.12.30. Last-resort condition: package is fully isolated from production code paths, present in the tree but never loaded. Remove when @modelcontextprotocol/sdk pins @hono/node-server ^2 itself.
overridesNotes.hono: Clears 11 hono advisories. The original 8 (GHSA-88fw-hqm2-52qc CORS wildcard-with-credentials, GHSA-hvrm-45r6-mjfj + GHSA-w62v-xxxg-mg59 jsx/cx XSS and cross-request leakage, GHSA-wwfh-h76j-fc44 serve-static traversal, plus the Lambda/ALB adapter set) and GHSA-8j4g-w8fx-2239 (CORS ReDoS, <4.12.34) are joined by three more that hit the previously pinned 4.12.34, so that pin had in turn gone stale and was holding the vulnerability — the same failure mode this note has now recorded twice: GHSA-gqvv-2mrq-wpjv (toSSG() still writes files outside the output directory, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-39408), GHSA-g6gw-c38x-mqfc (unbounded dot-notation nesting in parseBody() causing memory exhaustion) and GHSA-crvj-82cr-hjcx (the query parser reads parameters after the URL fragment, creating cache-key and proxy interpretation differentials), all vulnerable <4.13.5 and all reported as moderate. Raised to 4.13.7, which @modelcontextprotocol/sdk's own ^4.11.4 already admits — so this stays a maturity CAP inside the parent's tested range, not a forced upgrade. 4.13.7 published 2026-09-04, 14 days old, clearing the 7-day quarantine unaided: no escape hatch was needed this time and .npmrc / pnpm-workspace.yaml were NOT modified. 4.13.8 exists but is 4 days old and inside the quarantine, which is exactly what the cap is for. Note hono has two parents (the SDK directly and @hono/node-server), so this is deliberately unscoped to cover both. Remove this pin at the next dependency review — once the newest in-range hono is comfortably mature, the SDK's own ^4.11.4 range resolves it correctly with no override at all.
overridesNotes.brace-expansion: SECURITY: clears GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp (DoS, exponential-time expansion of consecutive non-expanding {} groups, <5.0.7) and GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (DoS, unbounded expansion length causing an OOM process crash, <5.0.8), both reported as high against the previously locked 5.0.6. Sole path is minimatch@10.2.5 -> brace-expansion, and minimatch declares ^5.0.5, so the patched 5.0.8 is already inside the parent's range — this is NOT a forced upgrade. The pin exists because it is simultaneously a maturity CAP: the newest release is 5.0.9, published 2 days before this pin and inside the 7-day quarantine, and refreshing the entry required the same per-command --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 escape hatch described in the @babel/generator note (the already-locked @rollup/rollup-* family re-validating), which would otherwise have admitted 5.0.9. Raised again to 5.0.9, which additionally clears GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation, vulnerable >=4.0.0 <5.0.9) — the 5.0.8 pin had in turn gone stale and was holding that one. Installed with a one-shot --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 at Betty's explicit request: 5.0.9 published 2026-07-30 and was 6.4 days old, just inside the 7-day quarantine; the guards were NOT modified. Safe to leave unscoped here because minimatch@10.2.5 is the only copy in this tree and declares ^5.0.5 — there is no 1.x/2.x consumer that a bare 5.x pin could break with the export-shape TypeError. This REPLACES the older 'brace-expansion@>=5.0.0 <5.0.6' pin, which had become inert — it only rewrote versions nothing would select while the lockfile sat on a vulnerable 5.0.6. Remove when minimatch's own ^5.0.5 resolves >=5.0.9 with no override.
overridesNotes.fast-uri@>=3.0.0 <3.1.6: SECURITY: clears four fast-uri advisories reported as high against the previously pinned 3.1.5, all fixed in 3.1.6 — GHSA-5jgf-p345-68v8 (host confusion via skipped IDN canonicalization on scheme-relative references, >=3.1.3 <3.1.6), GHSA-fph4-wmhf-6fwf (SSRF via repeated hostname percent-decoding, >=3.1.2 <3.1.6), GHSA-f65p-4m7j-42xc (SSRF via malformed IPv6 normalization, >=3.0.0 <3.1.6) and GHSA-jqff-g426-hqxp (host confusion via percent-encoded scheme normalization, >=3.0.0 <3.1.6). The previous '<3.1.5 -> 3.1.5' pin had gone stale and was itself holding the vulnerable version, so both the range key and the target moved. Sole path is apps/web -> @modelcontextprotocol/sdk -> ajv -> fast-uri, and ajv@8 declares ^3.0.1, so 3.1.6 is already inside the parent's range — a resolution pin, not a forced upgrade. Still scoped to the 3.x line rather than a bare key ON PURPOSE: fast-uri 4.x is a separate major (4.2.1 is current) that ajv's ^3.0.1 cannot accept, so a flat 'fast-uri' override would break ajv's declared range outright. 3.1.6 published 2026-08-23, 27 days old, clearing the 7-day quarantine unaided — .npmrc and pnpm-workspace.yaml were NOT modified. Remove when ajv's own ^3.0.1 resolves >=3.1.6 with no override.
overridesNotes.ip-address: SECURITY: clears three SSRF / trust-boundary bypasses reported as high+moderate against the locked 10.2.0 — GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (high: Address4 decodes leading-zero octets as decimal while resolvers decode them as octal), GHSA-22jq-vg5j-6vgg (IPv4-mapped/NAT64 misclassification) and GHSA-4xrf-jv44-h6hh (a CIDR suffix suppresses special-use classification). All three are fixed by 10.3.1. Sole path is @modelcontextprotocol/sdk -> express-rate-limit -> ip-address, and express-rate-limit declares ^10.2.0, so 10.3.1 is already inside the parent's range — this is NOT a forced upgrade, only a resolution pin, and no parent upgrade is needed. Deliberately unscoped so no vulnerable copy can appear under a future parent. Relevance is direct rather than theoretical: this is a scanner that classifies and fetches untrusted addresses, which is exactly the trust boundary these advisories bypass. 10.3.1 is 10 days old, clearing the 7-day quarantine. Remove when express-rate-limit's own ^10.2.0 resolves >=10.3.1 with no override.
overridesNotes.express>qs: SECURITY: clears GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g (DoS via an attacker-controlled isBuffer, >=2.2.5 <6.16.0) and GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx (array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing, >=6.14.2 <=6.15.3), both reported as moderate against the locked 6.15.2 and both fixed in 6.16.0. Sole path is apps/web -> @modelcontextprotocol/sdk -> express -> qs, and express@5.2.1 declares qs ^6.14.0, so 6.16.0 is already inside the parent's range — a resolution pin, not a forced upgrade, and no SDK upgrade is needed to clear it. Scoped to express rather than a bare key because express is the only consumer in this tree and a flat key would rewrite any future copy resolving on a different line. Relevance is direct: qs parses the query string of every request @modelcontextprotocol/sdk's Express transport serves. 6.16.0 published 2026-08-29, 20 days old, clearing the 7-day quarantine unaided — .npmrc and pnpm-workspace.yaml were NOT modified. Remove when express's own ^6.14.0 resolves >=6.16.0 with no override.
overridesNotes.@babel/generator: Maturity CAP, not a security fix — no advisory here. Covers the whole 2026-08-01 batch: @babel/generator, @babel/parser, @babel/traverse, @babel/types, browserslist>baseline-browser-mapping and browserslist>electron-to-chromium. eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1 depends on @babel/core ^7.24.4, which pulls the @babel/* siblings and (via browserslist) the two browser-data packages — all NEW to this tree. @babel/core resolved to a mature 7.29.7, but its own ^7.29.7 sibling ranges resolved to 7.29.8, published under 24h earlier. This is the same trap the jsdom>undici note describes: adding the lint plugins required a per-command --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 to get past the already-locked, already-vetted @rollup/rollup-*@4.62.3 family (6 days old, re-validated only because any package.json edit forces a full re-resolution), and that global escape hatch would otherwise have admitted six sub-2-day-old packages. 7.29.7 is 68 days old and satisfies @babel/core's ^7.29.7, so this stays inside the parent's tested range rather than forcing a version on it — and it dedupes the tree, since @babel/parser and @babel/types were ALREADY present at 7.29.7 and had gained a second 7.29.8 copy. The two browserslist children are scoped to their only consumer and sit inside its ^1.5.393 / ^2.10.44 ranges. .npmrc and pnpm-workspace.yaml are untouched. Remove all six at the next dependency review, once these versions are comfortably mature and the parents' own ranges resolve them with no override at all.

overridesNotes.esbuild@>=0.27.0 <0.28.1: GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr — the esbuild dev server allows arbitrary file read when run on Windows (vulnerable >=0.27.3 <0.28.1), reported as low against the locked 0.27.7. Two consumers: vitest -> vite@8.1.5 -> esbuild, and tsup -> bundle-require@5.1.0. vite peers ^0.27.0 || ^0.28.0 and bundle-require peers >=0.18, so 0.28.1 is inside BOTH declared ranges — a resolution pin, not a forced upgrade. Keyed on the range rather than a bare 'esbuild' ON PURPOSE: a flat key would also rewrite the 0.25.12 copy that the @esbuild-kit/core-utils entry deliberately pins for drizzle-kit, undoing that note. Dev-only, and Windows-only while the runtime is a Linux container, so this is hygiene rather than live exposure. 0.28.1 published 2026-06-11, 62 days old. Remove when vite's own peer range resolves >=0.28.1 with no override.
